title: Maximum Number of Ones
summary: Given a matrix M with dimensions width × height , where each cell contains either 0 or 1, and any square sub-matrix of size sideLength × sideLength contains no more than maxOnes ones, determine the maximum possible number of ones that the matrix M can have.
statement: Given a matrix M with dimensions width × height , where each cell contains either 0 or 1, and any square sub-matrix of size sideLength × sideLength contains no more than maxOnes ones, determine the maximum possible number of ones that the matrix M can have.
constraints: sideLength does not exceed width or height.
Every sideLength-square may contain at most maxOnes ones.
hints: A sideLength-by-sideLength pattern repeats safely across the whole matrix.
Count how often every residue pair modulo sideLength appears.
Choose the maxOnes residue positions with greatest frequencies.
Every constrained square contains each residue once, and periodic placement reaches the upper bound.
editorial: Every constrained square contains each residue once, and periodic placement reaches the upper bound.

tests.explanation: Choosing the most frequent residue position places four ones.
The two most frequent residue positions place six ones.
